summary: E: fresh (blob 315119e2 = mint, BEST 1.6904 unchanged). The mechanism is [shelf] (CLAIMS:99), whose reopen is 'ride on the next decode candidate'; running it standalone is waived by today's user steer (user-requested, below-bar, H100-derived first). Proceed with no companion, but re-derive the value case and change the readout. 44f30364 read in per-load speedup terms (the headline's own arithmetic) gave wh only +0.17% headline, not the ~+1.15% the row-us reading suggests: SGLang's in-run time also fell x0.959 at verify_32. A realistic gain is ~+0.8-1.1%, so p(beating the 1.24% margin) is ~0.3.
justification: A. The mechanism is sound and judge-proven where it matters. moe's wh5ds pair (wg_kernel<G,14>) read 92.8 vs wh 98.9 vs master 115.1 us on the judge (54b70249). moe's verify_32 load speedup went 2.121 -> 2.264 while SGLang's own time stayed flat (x1.007), so +1.08% headline came from T=256 alone: a clean transfer. Decode's 44f30364 proved the wh half in-run on the judge: bit-exact 16/16, isolated pair wh/m .898-.902 (T=128) and .838-.842 (T=256), whole-layer wh/m .973-.976 and .960-.979 under the real ea4x cold half. hh3 adds A5b+D+SC on top at x0.987/0.988 forked (node) and x0.967-0.973 isolated. WEAKEST LINK: the value case. value_gain 1.53% comes from hh3's H100 stand-in elasticities. Decode's own judge evidence says less. (1) The in-run FORK lines of 44f30364 put wh at T=256 -12.6 us and T=128 -8.4 us of layer time, which the same elasticities turn into ~+0.8%. wh5ds adds ~+0.2-0.4% (hh3 +0.21%; moe's judge pair wh5ds/wh .938 is better than the node's .973). Expect ~+1.0-1.1%, under the 1.24% margin. (2) The judged rows show even less once read as the headline computes it: per load, SGLang's in-run time over yours, geomean over 6 loads. In 44f30364 vs board 7cc034f9, the verify_32 load had SGLang x0.959 and yours x0.945, so the load speedup went 1.636 -> 1.659 (+0.24% headline). The verify_16 load had SGLang x0.984 and yours x0.988, so its speedup went 1.626 -> 1.619 (-0.07%). The 'verify_32 sliding 427.7 -> 403.2 us' reading (LOG 1954Z, CLAIMS:99) mostly measured a faster GPU draw: the baseline sped up 4% on the same rows. Net judged wh effect: +0.17% headline. The other four loads cost -0.77%: decode_1 -0.29%, decode_16 -0.38%, verify_1 -0.22%, decode_32 +0.07%. That is why the result read flat. T=128 shows ~0 judged transfer despite pair .90 and layer .975 in prepare. This fits CLAIMS:69 (prepare-time margins do not track judged rows) and the T=128 cold half being ~2-2.8x the hot. Expected shapes and directions match TASK: only verify_16/32 (T=128/256) run the hybrid, and decode_*/verify_1 should be flat in expectation. The prior field is honest: CLAIMS:99 is the same routed wh, now with the wh5ds arm. Nothing on FINDINGS' Do-not-try list blocks it. hothalf-a3-exactn-ring-wh is listed there as within-ci, but CLAIMS:99's newer [shelf] line supersedes that listing and names exactly this follow-up. Q (verify_16 profile, hot pair 69.6 -> 92.8 us vs in-run race .90): no red flag for the kernel. Per-kernel GPU time in this profile includes PDL and overlap waits (the profile footer says so; CLAIMS:53 / DISTILL:266 refuted sizing from such rows). Three readings of the same run show it. (a) In that same verify_16 sliding row, the cold ea4x pair fell 197.1 -> 130.9 us, so hot+cold fell 266.7 -> 223.7 while the row fell only 3.8 us. (b) On untouched rows, verify_1 full ea4x went 73.5 -> 107.6 us with the row flat (159.3 -> 158.5). (c) At verify_32 sliding, the cold pair rose 140.9 -> 182.7 while the hot pair fell 153.5 -> 122.8. So the hypothesis's own cited 'x0.80 hot pair' evidence is equally unreadable. The profile is also a single routing draw at T=128, where the hot set (> 16 routes per expert) varies a lot per draw. It is a yellow flag in one sense only: together with the flat verify_16 load speedup, it says T=128 bought nothing judged in 44f30364. Also, 92.8 numerically equals moe's T=256 wh5ds pair (92.8 us); the two are unrelated quantities, so do not conflate them.
confounders: v4xd-stack (CLAIMS:95; EAD4X_BOARD {16: 'd'} at submission.py:13976; arms at :12243). The T=16 ea4x pooled-hysteresis race drew v4cxs (ea4x_*_kernel<2,false>) on the board run 7cc034f9 and v4cxd (<2,true>, pdl & 256) in 44f30364 ('16:d>s D1.010 PASS(8) pooled near 6r'). decode_16 sliding moved 161.1 -> 169.5 us, and the decode_16 load cost -0.38% headline. This change does not touch that race, but it decides the headline as much as the hot half does. Read the [ea4x-dl] route line before the headline.

v4xd-stack fork guard / W6-M side-stream fork (CLAIMS:94-95, _sfk_gate). It sets how much of the hot cut surfaces through the fork. The wh phase runs before _sfk_gate, so the no-loss layer gate must hold in whichever mode _sfk_gate then picks. In 44f30364, fork and serial wh/m agreed within .002, so requiring both costs nothing.

pinned trim H-16 at T=128/256 (CLAIMS:69). It fixes the hot set, so it fixes the N distribution that exact-N and SC (N <= 32 only) see. Its lesson (prepare-time layer margins do not track judged rows) means the layer gate may only veto. It must not choose between wh and wh5ds.
Engine A v4x port (CLAIMS:93): the T=128 cold half is v4cxs at ~2-2.8x the hot pair. This is why T=128's hot cut hides (verify_16 load flat in 44f30364) and why T=128 is unlikely to add judged gain.

W6-B diet cells and W6-G fast silu in wg (CLAIMS:64, 68): they share the wg epilogue and the T>=128 launch sequence. Exact-N and SC change loop bounds and commit grouping. The torch.equal exactness gate on every routed class (as in 44f30364 and 54b70249) covers this; keep it.

hothalf-a3-exactn-ring-wh (CLAIMS:99, branch hyp/muse_decode_layer/hothalf-a3-exactn-ring-wh): this is the port's base for decode-specific plumbing, but it is not on master. This check therefore lands wh and wh5ds together, and one headline cannot split them. Only the in-run ROUTE line's wh5ds/wh pair ratio can.
interference: C. No companion. The two classes the change touches are two different loads (verify_16 = T=128, verify_32 = T=256), so the per-load speedups attribute the result per class directly. The in-run [hh-wh] lines (D0 fidelity, wh/m, wh5ds/wh, layer gate per class) separate kernel transfer from fork hiding. An ab-revert of any landed item would not sharpen a ~+1% effect against ~+-2% per-load drift. A T=256-only control (T=128 forced to master, as moe routed) is the one candidate. It is not warranted, because the per-load reading already isolates T=128. What the build and readout must do instead: (1) READ PER LOAD, as the headline does. Compute load speedup = in-run SGLang load time over yours, for verify_16 and verify_32, vs board 7cc034f9 (1.626 / 1.636) and vs 44f30364 (1.619 / 1.659). Do not read row us; SGLang's own time drifts x0.95-1.01 per load between runs. (2) Before the headline, report the T=16 ea4x route (board drew s; d cost ~-0.38% in 44f30364) and the T=1 draw (CLAIMS:unresolved T=1 lucky-draw line). (3) Use profile rows only to show that wg_kernel<G,14> (or <G,7>) ran per row, never for time (CLAIMS:53). (4) The layer gate is a veto only. The chosen arm's whole-layer ratio vs master must be <= 1.00 in every round, in both serial and fork modes. If wh5ds fails, fall back to wh if wh passes, else master. Never choose between wh and wh5ds on layer time; choose on the isolated pair (wh5ds <= 0.98 vs wh, every round, as moe did). Decision rule: a scored run only if the check beats 1.6904 by the 1.24% margin. Otherwise append a CLAIMS line with the per-load numbers: verify_32 load speedup up >= ~2% over the board with SGLang flat = T=256 transfer holds (carry it as a rider); verify_16 flat again = mark T=128 [unresolved] or refuted for the judged headline.
rules_flags: None blocking. x5 (A5b) re-encodes NVFP4 codes (ENC4 bit permutation) and packs E4M3 scale bytes as 7-bit b-8 fields. It is a lossless prepare-time bijection of the weights only, valid because every scale byte is scanned to lie in 0x08..0x7E (else OFF). TASK.md:102 permits lossless repacking, and moe passed the judge with the same encoding (54b70249, a5318a1f). Keep the scan, the inverse check per chunk and the host self-test (moe _wh_selftest).

kernel_fn dispatch must stay a dict lookup on the T class (a shape), with no branch on route counts, no host sync and no allocation, as in 44f30364. Exact-N/SC selection stays in-kernel from the chunk's nbk.

Memory and prepare: master bank + a3-permuted copy + x5 copy (~3 banks). Free the unrouted copies after routing. Judge prepare was 111.6 s in 44f30364 and moe's was 125.7 s on the node, so there is headroom under 300 s. Keep the 240 s phase guard.
freshness: E(i): no [refuted] or [superseded] claim on this mechanism. The newest line, CLAIMS:99 (wh hot half), is [shelf] with reopen 'ride as a bit-exact rider on the next decode candidate (with A5b+D+SC per hh3, ~+0.2%)'. This hypothesis is that rider run standalone. Under E's shelf rule it would need a >= 2.5% stack, which the user's 10-29 steer waives (user-requested, below-bar allowed, H100-derived work first); recorded as waived, not met. CLAIMS:98 (A3 [lead]) is its parent. CLAIMS:59 (wg2) and CLAIMS:72 (S1a) are refuted but are different mechanisms. CLAIMS:67 refuted the hot/cold fork inside decode's layer, and this keeps CAMPAIGN_HCF False, so it does not reopen it. E(ii): no landed claim owns verify_16/32 with a competing hot-half mechanism. CLAIMS:69 (pinned H-16) and CLAIMS:95 (v4xd-stack) are the base it builds on, both on master. E(iii): BEST 1.6904 (7cc034f917274439), master blob 315119e2 = mint blob, moved 0.00% against the 1.24% margin: fresh. The value case should still be re-derived from 44f30364's in-run FORK lines (~+0.8% wh, +0.2-0.4% wh5ds, so ~+1.0-1.1%, p ~0.3, EV ~0.3%), not hh3's +1.53% stand-in.
open_questions: Size: master is 955,413 B. 44f30364's wh module added 28,608 B net (984,021). moe's full wh/wh5ds module section is ~34.3 KB (muse_moe_w4a16/submission.py from '# ---- hothalf-wh-a5b-port'). A naive port lands near ~990-991 KB, over the 990,000 campaign line (DECISIONS:455), though under the 1,000,000 okc cap. Plan the trims up front so the result is <= ~988,500 B and leaves room for later riders (forkguard and the like): drop a3nx (already attributed in 44f30364); shrink the 2x2 FORK diagnostic to the veto gate (master vs routed arm, both modes); cut the step markers and dead diag text. Is the a3 arm still worth keeping as anything but a fallback? D0 is the only control that matters.

T=128: 44f30364's verify_16 load speedup was flat to slightly down (1.626 -> 1.619) with wh routed, despite pair .90 and layer .975 in prepare. moe kept T=128 on master. Should decode route T=128 at all, or carry it only if this run's verify_16 load speedup rises over the board with SGLang flat? Keeping it is cheap (bit-exact, no-loss veto). If it reads flat twice, retire it.

Does the judge's SGLang per-load drift (x0.959 at verify_32 in 44f30364; x0.949-1.008 across loads in moe) make any single-check verdict on a ~1% decode lever meaningful? If this reads flat again, the next read should be the scored-run pair or a rider on a larger decode candidate (CLAIMS:99's own reopen), not a third standalone check.

Should the T=16 ea4x race be pinned to the board's draw (v4cxs) in a separate determinism change? It cost ~-0.38% headline in 44f30364, more than this whole lever's T=128 share. That is out of scope here; keep this check's routing unchanged so it stays a clean port.

moe's no-loss gate timed kernel_fn T=256 with the fork as routed. Decode's analog is _ead_layer_gate per T class, in both _sfk_gate modes because the fork route is decided after this phase. Confirm that the builder runs the gate after the wh5ds/wh pair pick and gates the picked arm, not each arm.
